commands: kubectl get pods -n test-social-network -o wide; kubectl get events -n test-social-network --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -20

cd /tmp; kubectl get svc,ep -n test-social-network | awk '{print $1,$2,$3,$5}' | column -t; kubectl get deploy -n test-social-network -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.template.spec.containers[0].ports[*].containerPort}{"\n"}{end}'

cd /tmp; kubectl get svc -n test-social-network -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.ports[*].port}->{.spec.ports[*].targetPort} {.spec.selector}{"\n"}{end}'; kubectl get ep -n test-social-network | awk '$2=="<none>"'
kubectl patch svc user-service -n test-social-network --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":9090}]'; kubectl get ep user-service -n test-social-network
agent.summary:
The anomaly was a port misconfiguration on the `user-service` Service. Its `targetPort` was 9999, but the container listens on 9090. Requests routed through that Service would have failed to connect.

I patched `targetPort` to 9090. The endpoint now shows `10.244.1.135:9090`. I didn't send any test requests through the service.

All pods were Running with no restarts. No other Service had a port or selector problem. `media-frontend` maps port 8081 to 8080, which I took to be the stock setup, so I left it alone.
